Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the NexMart Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to NexMart Inc.'s Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, COO; Riley Patel, CMO; Morgan Chen, CTO; Casey Lopez, CDO; and Jordan Ellis, CSO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, CEO of NexMart Inc.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3 performance, driven by robust marketplace dynamics from our recent fee adjustments and accelerating gross merchandise value growth that outpaced our guidance. We saw significant growth in key metrics like active buyers and average order values across our core categories.

Our focus remains on optimizing seller economics to foster loyalty and volume in a competitive landscape. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our expanded private label offerings, which we believe will significantly enhance our margin profile through higher take rates and reduced reliance on low-margin third-party sales.

We are investing heavily in supply chain automation and AI-driven personalization to drive fulfillment efficiencies.

We are focused on improving customer acquisition through performance marketing and data-led campaigns.

We are expanding our presence in high-growth regions like APAC and emerging markets.

We are enhancing our customer experience through faster delivery options and seamless omnichannel integrations.

Finally, we are committed to sustainable practices that align with consumer preferences for eco-friendly shopping.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. Our Q3 revenue was $10.2 billion, an increase of 25% year-over-year. Gross margin was 42.5%, driven by a favorable product mix shift toward private label and supply chain optimizations that more than offset promotional pressures. Operating expenses were $3.8 billion, representing 37% of revenue. Our marketing investments yielded strong returns, with disciplined spend allocation across channels contributing to improved efficiency metrics.

Let's start with gross merchandise value, our core topline metric, which reached $28.7 billion for the quarter, up 22% year-over-year and 11% quarter-over-quarter. This was a strong beat against our guidance of 18-20% YoY and 8-10% QoQ, surpassing the midpoint by more than three percentage points annually and one point sequentially. Coming off Q2's $25.8 billion, this reflects solid seasonal momentum heading into the holidays and early wins from our NeoMart Accelerate program.

Regionally, North America, at 52% of GMV, posted $14.9 billion, up 25% YoY and 13% QoQ, exceeding our 20-22% guide thanks to 15% growth in monthly active buyers to 145 million and 8% higher AOV at $145, driven by same-day delivery expansions covering 85% of top U.S. markets via DoorDash and Uber Eats partnerships. Europe, 28% of GMV, hit $8.0 billion with 28% YoY and 12% QoQ growth, beating 22-25% expectations through GDPR-compliant AI recommendations boosting conversions 18% and new hubs like Warsaw cutting fulfillment costs 12%. APAC surged to $4.3 billion, 15% of total, with 45% YoY and 14% QoQ gains that crushed our 35-40% guide, propelled by $1.2 billion from live commerce in Southeast Asia and 22 million buyer adds in India and Indonesia. Rest of world added $1.5 billion, up 12% as guided, aided by buy-now-pay-later integrations.

This GMV decomposed into 10% from buyer growth with 28 million net adds, 7% from 12% higher frequency to 4.2 orders per buyer annually, and 5% from AOV, tempered by emerging market mix. Technically, edge computing for sub-100ms mobile loads cut abandonment 22%, ML forecasting reduced stockouts 35%, and eco-badges grew apparel 15%.

Shifting to one key driver: our late Q2 marketplace fee structure updates. We cut average referral fees from 15.2% to 11.8% in electronics, apparel, and home & garden—62% of GMV—added tiered ad credits for sellers over $100K quarterly, and capped NexFulfill fees at 18% from 22% to match Amazon FBA and Walmart. Data from our Seller Insights Dashboard on 2.5 million sellers guided this against Temu, Shein, and Shopify pressures.

Impacts were swift: 28% YoY new seller activations to 450,000 net adds, total active sellers at 2.8 million; 35% reactivations via AI campaigns. Listings per seller up 17% to 245 SKUs, favoring high-velocity items—electronics +22%, apparel -8%—lifting take rate to 12.4%, up 60 bps QoQ. Seller ACoS fell to 24% from 29% with dynamic NexAds ML on 1.2 billion clicks.

Quantitatively, third-party GMV hit $18.7 billion, +22% YoY, +5% QoQ; small sellers drove 41% vs. 35%; churn to 4.2% from 7.1%; GMV per seller $42K, +14%; top tier +31%; NexFulfill at 48%, +12 points, aiding 15% same-day uplift and 28% NexPrime lift.

North America saw 42% reactivations, 31% seller sales share; Europe 32% new sellers post-DMA with 10.5% VAT fees and cross-border upticks; APAC 41% growth undercutting Shopee; emerging added 18K sellers. Seller Studio 2.0 with AI forecasting (95% accuracy) and repricing gave 11% GMV uplift for adopters; blockchain pilots cut fraud 27%. Seller services revenue +29% to $2.1B offset fee cuts for 110 bps take rate gain. Q4 seller GMV guide 20-24% YoY.

On fulfillment cost per order, we hit $7.85, down 12% YoY from $8.92 and 4% sequentially from $8.18—10th straight quarter of declines, -14% three-year CAGR from $10.50. As 8.2% of GMV vs. 11.5% prior, it added 120 bps to margins, beating peers at $9-11.

Breakdown: shipping/last-mile 58% ($4.55), pick-pack 24% ($1.88), inbound 12% ($0.94), overhead 6% ($0.47). Post-2021 peak of $12.20, we've trended down despite diesel +7% and wages +5.2%. Automation hit 85% of 28 NA FCs with AMRs, cutting cycle times 32%, saving $0.45/order ($28M quarterly). AI routing on 2.5B orders dropped misroutes 22%, rates 14%; micro-FCs cut miles 30%, last-mile 18%; right-sizing saved $0.12, returns 15%. U.S. $6.50 (-15%), Europe $9.20 (-8%), APAC $11.00 (-5%). FY24 guide $7.90-$8.00, FY25 mid-$7s on $450M capex.

Gross margins expanded to 42.5%, +240 bps YoY from 40.1% and +110 bps QoQ—sixth straight quarter, +650 bps over two years from 36% trough amid freight spikes. Outperforms peers at 38-40%.

Mix: private label 28% of GMV (from 18%), 55-60% GM vs. 35-40% third-party; Nova Essentials +45%, ASP +8% to $52; home/garden 48%, electronics 44%, apparel 38%. Supply chain: inbound -12% to $4.20 via nearshoring; robotics FCs pick-pack -18% to $2.80; last-mile -10%; returns 14% via CV. Promotions pressured 80 bps (22% discounts), labor/packaging 50 bps. NA 45.5%, Europe 39%, APAC 41%. Q3 guide 43.0-43.5%, year-end 44%.

Net income was $285 million, +28% YoY from $222 million, beating $240M guide and $255M consensus; adjusted $292M. Diluted EPS $0.92, +31% from $0.70, above $0.78-$0.82 guide and $0.84 Street by 10%; adjusted $0.95.

Topline $10.2B revenue +25%, GMV $28.7B +22%, buyers +12% to 145M, AOV $85 steady via NexAI upsells. Margins +210 bps; take rate 16.1%; fulfillment/unit -8% to $4.20. SG&A efficient, marketing 11.5% of revenue, CAC $22, LTV:CAC 4.2x; NexPrime 65M members, $1.2B recurring. U.S. $177M (+35%), Europe $68M (+15%), APAC $28M flat, emerging $12M. Headwinds: freight +5%, forex -$8M, restructuring $15M. Q3 EPS guide $0.98-$1.05 above $0.96 consensus; FY $3.85-$3.95.

Marketing efficiency: blended CAC $42.30, -12% YoY from $48.10, -5% QoQ; ROAS 4.2x from 3.7x. Paid social 45% ($35 CAC, TikTok 5.8x); search $55 (3.9x); affiliate $28 (6.1x); organic $18. Paid/organic 62/38; LTV:CAC 3.8:1, LTV $165. NovaPredict AI +35% incrementality; server-side post-ATT; UID2.0. NA $48, Europe $36, APAC $29. Q3 CAC ~$40, ROAS 4.5x.

Ad spend ROAS 4.8x, +12% YoY; $120M spend generated $576M revenue (28% GMV). Search 7.2x (35%), social 3.9x (28%, TikTok 3.2x), retail media 5.6x (22%), display 2.8x. NA 5.4x, Europe 4.1x, APAC 3.6x. Vertex AI LTV bidding, first-party data 65%; Q3 5.0-5.2x.

Campaigns: awareness US 42% aided (+25%), global 18% unaided (+30%); 1.2M new customers (+15%), CAC $45 (-10%). TikTok 350K at $32; influencers 150K at 6.1x. CDP 92% match; CTV pilots. NA 650K, Europe 220K, APAC 280K. LTV $320, 4:1 ratio.

We are reaffirming our full-year guidance of revenue $38-40 billion, adjusted EPS $3.85-$3.95.

Now I'll turn it over to Taylor Kim to discuss operations.

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, Jordan. Operationally, we focused on network densification and robotics scaling. Our shipping times improved by 25%. Fulfillment costs were down 12% per order. We are implementing AI sortation in all major FCs.

Now I'll turn it over to Riley Patel.

Riley Patel:
Thanks, Taylor. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from TikTok Shop integrations and influencer micro-campaigns. Customer acquisition costs were $42, with ROAS at 4.8x. Our brand awareness increased by 25% in core markets. We are focusing on performance branding and CTV expansion.

Now I'll turn it over to Morgan Chen.

Morgan Chen:
Thanks, Riley. On the technology front, we've been focused on edge computing for mobile and ML demand forecasting. Our website uptime was 99.99%. Mobile app usage increased by 35%. We're investing in cookieless targeting with UID 2.0.

Now I'll turn it over to Casey Lopez.

Casey Lopez:
Thanks, Morgan. Data science is a key focus for us. We've seen a 18% improvement in conversion rates because of SmartRecs personalization. We are also focusing on privacy-safe clean rooms.

Now I'll turn it over to Jordan Ellis.

Jordan Ellis:
Thanks, Casey. Sustainability is very important to us. We reduced our carbon footprint by 27% through reusable packaging and nearshoring. We are committed to EcoScore badges and drone delivery offsets.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question and answer session. [Operator instructions for Q&A session]. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Can you expand on the GMV acceleration and how sustainable it is into Q4?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, John. The 22% YoY and 11% QoQ GMV beat was broad-based, with buyer adds, frequency, and AOV all contributing. Sustainability comes from our Accelerate initiative—AI recs, live commerce in APAC, and delivery expansions. We're raising Q4 to 24-27% YoY, confident in holiday momentum.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen:
Great, thanks. On net income and EPS outperforming—any color on the drivers and FY outlook?

Jordan Lee:
Emily, the $285 million net income and $0.92 EPS beat came from revenue momentum, 42.5% margins, and opex discipline. Regional strength in NA and Europe, plus NexPrime recurring revenue. FY guide up to $3.85-$3.95 reflects AI efficiencies and easier comps.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan.

Mike Rodriguez:
Thanks. Thoughts on fulfillment cost trends and further improvements?

Taylor Kim:
Mike, $7.85 FCPO decline ties to 85% AMR coverage, AI routing, and micro-FCs—saving $0.45/order from robotics alone. Regional variances, but FY25 mid-$7s on G2P and drones. Balanced with 98.2% OTIF.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Barclays.

Lisa Wong:
Impressive marketing efficiency. Can you detail CAC and ROAS by channel?

Riley Patel:
Lisa, blended CAC $42.30 with 4.2x ROAS—TikTok 5.8x standout, affiliates 6.1x. Social and search optimized via NovaPredict; shift to owned channels. Q3 trends to $40 CAC, 4.5x ROAS on CTV ramp.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Citi.

David Kim:
On tech—how is the fee update impacting seller tech adoption?

Morgan Chen:
David, Seller Studio 2.0 with 95% accurate AI forecasting and daily repricing on 500M comps drove 11% GMV uplift for 15% adopters. Blockchain fraud cuts and dynamic bidding ACoS to 24%. Edge tech supports this scale.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Patel with Deutsche Bank.

Rachel Patel:
Data side—conversion lifts and privacy efforts?

Casey Lopez:
Rachel, 18% conversion via SmartRecs on 500M SKUs; server-side tracking post-ATT holds 92% match. Clean rooms enable LTV bidding; incrementality tests validate 25% social lift.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Ellis with RBC Capital.

Tom Ellis:
Sustainability—how does it tie to seller behavior and margins?

Jordan Ellis:
Tom, EcoScore on 40% listings grew categories 15%; reusable totes and nearshoring cut footprint 27%. Ties to seller loyalty—platinum tier access—and 120 bps margin from packaging savings.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
